A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Value Flows, with matching authors, core methods, theory, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original return-distribution measurements, OGBench and D4RL evaluations, offline-to-online learning curves, and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds resource measurements, a risk-sensitive MDP experiment, and further policy and loss ablations.

M1.justification: The principal algorithm, DCFM/BCFM objectives, and uncertainty weighting remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds a discrete-action adaptation that replaces learned policy extraction with greedy CVaR-based action selection. Appendix D.5 tests a Gaussian BC policy variant. These are limited procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: The existing OGBench, D4RL, and offline-to-online task coverage is retained. Appendix D.4 adds an 11-state Machine Replacement MDP with stochastic rewards and risk-sensitive control requirements. The expanded trajectory description in Section 5.1 documents the existing Figure 2 evaluation rather than establishing another newly tested scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the principal evaluations is unchanged. The new Machine Replacement comparison includes Q-learning alongside C51 and IQN (Figure 11). Appendix E.2's expanded descriptions of C51/IQN policy extraction do not establish changes to their existing implementations.

E3.justification: New protocols include CVaR_0.1 evaluation using 100,000 random-policy transitions with uniformly initialized states, resource measurements, and policy/loss controls. Figure 7 extends the flow-step sweep with one and two steps. IFQL candidate counts change from 32 to 128 for door-cloned and relocate-human, and from 128 to 32 for hammer-human (v1 Table 4; v2 Table 6). These reported setting changes do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the earlier component ablations, v2 expands low-step sensitivity testing and adds resource profiling, a risk-sensitive case study, Gaussian-versus-flow policy extraction, and BCFM-only/DCFM-only loss comparisons (Appendices D.3–D.6). These substantially expand evidence about computational cost, applicability, and which components supply the learning signal.

E5.justification: Appendix D.4 specifies four seeds for the new state-based risk experiment, adding a distinct replication setting to the retained eight-seed state-based benchmark protocol. Existing benchmark means, standard deviations, and eight/four-seed reporting remain. No increase in existing run counts or new significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the offline-to-online results are unchanged. In the full offline table, Value Flows changes from 66±4 to 67±9 on pen-human and from 102±2 to 105±3 on relocate-expert (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3). Substantial new results include low-step failures, resource costs, CVaR convergence, approximately 10% improvement with Gaussian BC on expert Adroit tasks, and near-zero BCFM-only success. These are additional findings, not a general improvement in the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendices A and B retain the mathematical definitions, propositions, lemmas, and proofs. The new notation table summarizes existing mathematics. Equation 17 aligns its target-field symbol with the replacement already described in v1; the expanded collapse discussion supplies explanatory motivation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: flow-based return distributions, the distributional Bellman objective, variance estimation, and uncertainty weighting. The headline 1.3x performance claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through target-network collapse avoidance (C.1), a policy/data-mismatch explanation for Adroit performance (D.5), and identification of DCFM as the main learning signal (D.6). It qualifies flow-step robustness and removes the characterization of visual tasks as partially observable. However, E.2 newly calls the uncertainty epistemic, conflicting with Section 4.3's retained aleatoric interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 documents the FQL-generated trajectories underlying Figure 2, exact offline-to-online task identifiers, C51/IQN action-selection implementations, and Value Flows hyperparameter search ranges. Table 6 adds previously missing maze settings and online distillation coefficients. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the common architecture, hardware disclosures, and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: New citations support target-network stability, fitted Q-learning, risk-sensitive control, and policy modeling, including Grill et al., Tian et al., Riedmiller, Keramati et al., and Dong et al. The target-network discussion adds a connection to self-supervised collapse avoidance, while the principal related-work positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained, with targeted expansions in Sections 4.2 and 5.1 and the practical-method appendix. Appendix D becomes Additional Experiments, the confidence-weight discussion moves into D.2, and experiment details move from F to E. Conference headers and an author-order footnote are added.

P2.justification: v2 adds notation Table 2 and Figures 10–13, expands Figure 7's curves and caption, and restructures the domain-specific hyperparameter table with additional rows and a distillation column. Existing result tables and figures are relocated and reflowed. These constitute substantial display additions beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new loss-isolation and Gaussian-policy ablations clarify previously underexamined design choices, while additional experimental details improve reproducibility. The principal benchmark evidence and proofs remain largely unchanged. Gains are tempered by new inconsistencies: Appendix D.3 claims lower GPU memory than FBRAC although Figure 10 shows higher usage, and E.2's epistemic-uncertainty description conflicts with Section 4.3. Overall, the added diagnostic evidence provides a limited net improvement.
